explanationHtml:
Fertiloscopy helps in obtaining a good view of the posterior surface (and not the anterior surface) of the ovary and genital organs. This is an advantage of fertiloscopy over laparoscopy.

The other advantages of fertiloscopy over laparoscopy are:

  • The Trendelenburg position is not needed. The procedure can be done in a lithotomy position
  • Trauma can be avoided as no trocar is needed
  • No CO2: Hydroperitoneum with saline
  • Peritoneal spill can be seen

Fertiloscopy is a new mini-invasive diagnostic technique that allows the visualization of the posterior pelvis. In this technique, an optical device is introduced into the pouch of Douglas, through the posterior vaginal fornix, under general/local anaesthesia.

It can also be used for small interventions, such as adhesiolysis, ovarian drilling, coagulation of endometriosis spots and to perform chromosalpingoscopy and salpingoscopy. With fertiloscopy, surgical intervention can be avoided and it is a good alternative to diagnostic laparoscopy.

question: Which the following are not the advantages of fertiloscopy over laparoscopy?

explanationHtml:
In the given clinical scenario, the next step in management will be hysteroscopy and laparoscopy-guided surgery.

Tubal contractions, particularly cornual spasms, can give an incorrect impression of proximal fallopian tube obstruction (a false-positive result) on hysterosalpingography. Laparoscopy with chromotubation is therefore considered to confirm the diagnosis of cornual spasm. Laparoscopy is both diagnostic and therapeutic in this condition.

Hysteroscopy is an operative procedure that provides an endoscopic view of the endometrial cavity and tubal ostia via the cervix, performed in the preovulatory phase. It can be diagnostic or therapeutic. It is the gold standard investigation for visualizing the uterine cavity and tubal ostia.

Therapeutic indications of hysteroscopy Diagnostic indications of hysteroscopy
  • Uterine septum
  • Asherman syndrome
  • Retained IUCD
  • Polypectomy
  • Submucous fibroid
  • Abnormal uterine bleeding
  • Tubal sterilization using sclerosing agents
  • To study the endocervical mucosal lining
  • Congenital malformations of the uterus
  • Endometrial tuberculosis
  • Misplaced IUCD
  • Endometrial lesions
  • Endometrial polyp
  • Asherman syndrome
  • Cornual tubal blockage

Contraindications to hysteroscopy are as follows:

  • Acute genital infections like genital herpes
  • A live intrauterine pregnancy
  • During menstruation, the view is obscured, and the infection rate is high.
  • Scarred uterus and enlarged uterus of size ≥ 12 weeks are relative contraindications.
  • Cervical stenosis can cause cervical tears and uterine perforation.
  • Cardiopulmonary disorder due to increased risk of fluid overload and pulmonary edema.
  • Diagnosed cervical malignancies

Laparoscopy is the gold standard for the evaluation of tubal factors in infertility, commonly done in the proliferative phase. It can be diagnostic or therapeutic.

Diagnostic Therapeutic (Operative)
  • Age >35 years
  • History of pelvic pain, dyspareunia, pelvic surgery, adhesions
  • Abnormal HSG
  • Failure to conceive after a reasonable period (6 months) with normal HSG
  • Women with comorbid pelvic pathology (PID, endometriosis)
  • Unexplained infertility
  • Reconstructive tubal surgery
  • Adhesiolysis
  • Fulguration of endometriotic implants
  • Ovarian drilling in PCOS
  • GIFT and ZIFT procedures

Benefits of laparoscopic evaluation:

  • Tubes: For detection of tubal patency, block (site and side), motility, hydrosalpinx change, peritubal adhesions, fimbrial agglutination
  • Ovaries: PCOS changes, endometriosis, PID, adhesions
  • Uterus: Anomalies, fibroids
  • Peritoneal factors: Adhesions, PID, endometriosis, tuberculosis
  • Therapy at the same sitting (as appropriate)
question: A 26-year-old woman underwent a workup for primary infertility. On hysterosalpingography, there was a bilateral cornual block. What is the next step in management?

correctAnswer: D. Human menopausal gonadotrophin, followed by hCG
explanationHtml:
The best line of management for the given patient is human menopausal gonadotropin (hMG) followed by hCG.

The patients who have undergone hypophysectomy i.e. removal of the pituitary gland, can not produce endogenous gonadotropins. Exogenous gonadotropins such as hMG are given to such patients. Timed administration of hCG is needed to induce ovulation after the follicle has matured.

The human menopausal gonadotropin is an extract of urine from postmenopausal women. It contains FSH and LH in the required ratio for follicular growth.

Clomiphene, letrozole, and GnRH analogs stimulate the release of gonadotropins from the pituitary gland. These are not helpful in a patient whose pituitary gland has been removed.

options.text: Human menopausal gonadotrophin, followed by hCG

lessonTitle: Perimenopause, Menopause And Post Menopausal Bleeding
question: Menopause is defined as cessation of menses for a period of _____.

correctAnswer: A. On day 2-5 after last menstrual period
explanationHtml:
The follicular stimulating hormone (FSH) level is studied on day 2–5 after the last menstrual period to detect the premenopausal stage.

It is a period of 3–4 years before menopause and is associated with mild ovarian hormonal deficiency leading to menstrual disorders, especially menorrhagia.

The climacteric phase is the phase of waning of ovarian activity. It begins 2 to 3 years before menopause and may continue 2-5 years after menopause. It marks the transition from active to inactive ovarian function and involves physical, sexual, and psychological adjustments.

The predictors of approaching menopause include:

  • A fall in the level of inhibin B and a corresponding rise in FSH level
  • A fall in the level of anti-Mullerian hormone (AMH) - This is a better marker of ovarian reserve and can be tested on any day of the cycle.

The average age of menopause in India is 47 years, and ranges from 45 to 50 years.

Menopause sets in when the follicle number falls below 1000. If this happens before 40 years, it is termed premature menopause while attaining it after 55 years is delayed menopause.

The age at which menopause is attained is not related to age at menarche, race, number of pregnancies, socio-economic status, or oral contraceptive pills usage. However, it is directly influenced by smoking and genetic disposition.

Norepinephrine and serotonin are responsible for hot flushes in menopausal women.

A fall in the level of estrogen causes a reduction in hypothalamic endorphins. This causes a release of more norepinephrine and serotonin, which lower the set point in the thermoregulatory nucleus. As a result, the heat-loss mechanism is triggered by even subtle changes in core body temperature.

Risk factors for hot flushes:

  • Low estradiol levels
  • High BMI
  • Sedentary lifestyle
  • Surgical menopause has increased risk
  • Low socioeconomic status
  • History of premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD)
  • Depression.

question: A menopausal woman presents with complaints of hot flushes. Which of the following neurotransmitters are responsible for these symptoms?

explanationHtml:
The clinical features are suggestive of vasomotor symptoms (hot flushes) in a menopausal woman for which the most effective treatment is hormonal therapy.

The principal hormone used in hormonal therapy is estrogen. Estrogen therapy is the most effective therapy for a woman with no uterus . In a woman with an intact uterus, only estrogen therapy can increase the risk of endometrial hyperplasia and endometrial carcinoma. Combined estrogen and progesterone therapy provides better protection against endometrial cancer.

Vasomotor symptoms of menopause like hot flushes can be managed by following methods:
1.Life style changes like weight loss, non-sweat-inducing exercise, mindfulness, stress reducing therapies, acupuncture, yoga, wellness education classes, hypnosis and cognitive behavioral therapy
2.Hormonal therapy like estrogen therapy, estrogen with progesterone therapy, bazedoxifene
3.Nonhormonal agents like selective serotonin-reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) and serotonin norepinephrine-reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs), gabapentinoids (gabapentin and pregabalin), and clonidine.

Option A: Even though combined OCPs contain both estrogen and progesterone, for treatment of hot flushes, a lesser dosage of each component is required.

Option B: Clonidine is an alpha 2 adrenergic agonist, it is used to reduce the severity and duration of hot flashes when estrogen is contraindicated like hypertensive patients.

Option D: Danazol is a synthetic androgen that inhibits gonadotropin production via feedback inhibition of the pituitary-ovarian axis . It can be used in treatment of endometriosis, hereditary angioedema.

question: A 53-year-old woman presents with episodes of sensation of intense heat involving the face and upper chest which rapidly spreads across the entire body. The episodes last about 2-4 minutes and are associated with profuse sweating. What is the most effective treatment for her?

explanationHtml:
The clinical scenario is suggestive of atrophic vaginitis. The next step in management should be topical estrogen therapy such as the estradiol-releasing vaginal ring.

Atrophic vaginitis is a common cause of post-menopausal bleeding due to low estradiol levels. Patients may present with dry vagina, dyspareunia and a purulent or blood-tinged discharge. The vagina appears pale, dry, and may show petechiae.

Treatment of atrophic vaginitis involves topical estrogens in the form of creams, tablets, or rings. Estrogen replacement restores vaginal mucosal elasticity, vaginal fluid secretion levels, blood flow, and sensorimotor responses.

Systemic therapy may help prevent recurrence. Vaginal lubricants and moisturizers can be given for symptomatic relief.

explanationHtml:
Hypertension is not a contraindication for hormone replacement therapy (HRT). HRT can be initiated in patients with a history of hypertension, diabetes, or smoking; provided they are regularly monitored.

Contraindications of estrogen therapy:

  • Breast cancer, uterine cancer, or family history of cancer
  • Previous history of thromboembolic episode
  • Liver and gall bladder diseases
  • Uterine fibroids - as the fibroids may enlarge in size.

question: Which of the following is not a contraindication for estrogen therapy?

explanationHtml:
Breast cancer developing subsequent to HRT is of low grade and has a good prognosis.

The risk of breast cancer is not increased up to 3 years of HRT and 5 years of estrogen-only replacement therapy. Lower risk is seen with the use of dydrogesterone in HRT.

HRT can cause recurrence of breast cancer and is, therefore, contraindicated in a woman who has been treated for breast cancer.

HRT increases the density of breast tissue and subsequently impedes the screening for breast cancer with mammography.

explanationHtml:
Endometrial biopsy is the investigation of choice in a case of post-menopausal bleed, as the chances of endometrial cancer are quite high.

For those who undergo TVUS and have an EEC (endometrial echo complex) >4 mm, localized thickening, or an indistinct or nonvisible EEC, endometrial sampling is a reasonable next step.

Investigations for endometrial carcinoma include:

  • Transvaginal ultrasound is the first investigation in abnormal uterine bleeding, especially in females >35 years and acts as an adjunct to endometrial biopsy.
  • Hysteroscopy and fractional curettage is the gold standard method to diagnose endometrial carcinoma.
  • Endometrial biopsy is the investigation of choice for endometrial cancer.
  • Pap smear is not reliable to diagnose endometrial carcinoma. It is more useful as a screening tool rather than a diagnostic tool.
  • Surgical staging is the gold standard investigation for staging endometrial carcinoma.

If symptoms of postmenopausal bleeding persist, imaging of the endometrial cavity should be performed with one or a combination of the following: TVUS, contrast sonography, or hysteroscopy.

question: What is the investigation of choice in a 55-year-old woman who presents with post-menopausal bleed?

explanationHtml:
Visualization of a mass with a single feeding vessel on a color Doppler is characteristic of an endometrial polyp. In contrast, submucous leiomyomas often receive blood flow from multiple vessels (option A).

Endometrial polyps are soft, fleshy growths within the uterus that consist of endometrial glands, fibrous stroma, and surface epithelium. Risk factors for endometrial polyps include increasing age, obesity, and tamoxifen use.

They are usually asymptomatic. When symptomatic, they present with heavy menstrual bleeding, prolonged bleeding, intermenstrual bleeding, or infertility.

The main diagnostic tools for endometrial polyps include transvaginal ultrasound (TVS) with applied color Doppler, saline infusion sonography, and hysteroscopy.

The risk factors for the malignant transformation include postmenopausal status, age older than 60, and abnormal bleeding. Other factors such as larger polyp size (>1.5 cm), tamoxifen use, diabetes, and obesity may also contribute to a higher risk.

Hysteroscopic polypectomy may be considered most effective for symptomatic women or those with risk factors for malignant transformation.

explanationHtml:
Normal saline is the ideal fluid media used for bipolar electrocautery as it can function regardless of the fluid electrolyte content.

Normal saline and lactated Ringer solutions are commonly used isotonic, electrolyte-containing fluids in operating rooms for diagnostic hysteroscopy procedures. These solutions can cause volume overload and, if rapidly absorbed in large volumes, may lead to pulmonary edema.

Isotonic, electrolyte-containing fluids are contraindicated for use with monopolar electrosurgical devices because they conduct electrical current, dissipate instrument energy and render the instrument ineffective. Low-viscosity, electrolyte-poor fluids such as 1.5-percent glycine, 3-percent sorbitol, and 5-percent mannitol are preferred as they are non-conductive and can be safely used with monopolar electrosurgical energy devices.

The primary risk of using hypotonic, hypoosmolar solutions is the intravascular absorption of these fluids, which can lead to acute hyponatremia and hypo osmolality.

The criteria for terminating the procedure for electrolyte-deficient fluid is a deficit of 1 L and electrolyte-rich fluid is a deficit of 2.5 L.

question: Which is the most common type of ovarian tumor?

explanationHtml:
BRCA 1 is the most carcinogenic gene in ovarian cancer.

5–10% of malignant ovarian tumors are genetic. BRCA 1 is associated with hereditary breast-ovarian cancer syndrome.

BRCA 1 is on chromosome 17q and BRCA 2 is on chromosome 13q.

MSH2 and MLH1 gene mutation is seen in hereditary non-polyposis colorectal cancer (HNPCC). It is associated with malignancy of the colon, ovary, and endometrium.
question: Which of the following is the most carcinogenic gene in ovarian cancer?

explanationHtml:
Bilateral tubectomy and hysterectomy reduce the risk of ovarian cancer.

Some ovarian malignancies originate in the fallopian tubes as dysplastic lesions which later spread to the ovary (dropping down theory). Thus, bilateral tubectomy reduces the risk of ovarian malignancy.

Risk factors for ovarian cancer:

  • Advancing age
  • Early menarche and late menopause
  • Talc exposure to the perineum
  • Family history of breast / ovarian cancer
  • Ovulation induction therapy by clomiphene citrate

Protective factors against ovarian cancer:

  • Use of oral contraceptive pills
  • Multiparity
  • Breastfeeding
  • Anovulation.
question: Which among the following reduces the risk of developing ovarian cancers?

explanationHtml:
Mucinous cystadenoma is the largest benign ovarian tumor.

Mucinous cystadenoma is a mucoid-containing, thick-walled cyst. It is usually multilocular and lined by single columnar epithelium.

It is the third most common epithelial tumor of the ovary. It has a 10% chance of becoming malignant. About 40% of dermoid cysts are found in conjunction with mucinous cystadenomas.
question: Which among the following is the largest benign ovarian tumor?

explanationHtml:
Stromal invasion is not seen in borderline ovarian tumors.

Borderline tumors of the ovary are classified under tumors of low malignant potential. The histological features of these tumors are intermediate between true benign lesions and invasive carcinomas. They are characterised by nuclear atypia, atypical epithelial proliferation, cellular pleomorphism but without stromal invasion.

Features of borderline ovarian tumors:

  • No stromal invasion
  • Mitotic figures <4/10 high power field
  • Survival rate is 90%
  • Usually occurs between 35-55 years of age
  • Serous type is the most common, followed by mucinous type.

Serous type is more common than mucinous type

question: Which of the following is false regarding borderline ovarian tumors?

correctAnswer: D. Follicular cyst is a benign epithelial tumor
explanationHtml:
Follicular cyst is a physiological/functional cyst of the ovary.

Physiological/functional cysts of the ovary:

  1. Follicular cyst - Failure of rupture of the follicle during ovulation.
  2. Theca lutein cyst - Stimulation of atretic follicles by abnormal HCG levels. It regresses when hCG levels fall.
  3. Luteoma of pregnancy - Due to prolonged elevation of hCG, like in multiple pregnancies.

Hemorrhagic ovarian cysts usually occur due to bleeding into the corpus luteum or other functional cysts at the time of ovulation. Hemorrhagic cysts are normal findings in ovulatory women, generally resolving within 8 weeks.

Cobweb appearance on USG in a hemorrhagic cyst is shown below.

Leutoma of pregnancy is associated with multiple pregnancy

question: Which of the following statements is false regarding ovarian cysts?

correctAnswer: B. The tumor would be immobile with an irregular surface
explanationHtml:
In Meig's syndrome, a benign ovarian mass is likely to be seen. Irregular surface and immobility are features of malignant tumors.

Meig’s syndrome is characterized by a triad of:

  1. Benign ovarian tumors
  2. Ascites
  3. Right-sided pleural effusion.

The pleural effusions are usually right-sided, even though the left-sided and bilateral effusions are possible.

Tumors causing Meigs' syndrome include ovarian fibroma, granulosa cell tumor, Brenner tumor, or thecoma.

However, when the causative factor is ovarian secondaries, leiomyoma, and benign ovarian cysts (such as teratoma and mucinous cystadenoma), the condition is called Pseudo Meigs' syndrome.

Resolution of ascites and pleural effusion is seen after the removal of the tumor.

Management:

  • Repeated paracentesis for ascites.
  • Unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy in young patients for preserving fertility
  • Total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (TAH-BSO) in postmenopausal women.

Note: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) patients may also have a combination of ascites, pleural effusion, and elevated serum levels of CA-125. This is known as Tjalma syndrome or pseudo-pseudo Meigs’ syndrome.

The tumor would be immobile with an irregular surface

question: Meigs' syndrome was suspected in a woman with right-sided pleural effusion, ascites, and an ovarian tumor. Which of the following statements is false regarding this condition?

explanationHtml:
Psammoma bodies are a histopathological finding of serous cystadenocarcinoma of the ovary.

They are calcified structures seen in areas of cellular degeneration. Their presence does not denote malignancy.

Psammoma bodies are seen in the following conditions:

  • Papillary carcinoma of the thyroid
  • Papillary serous carcinoma of the endometrium
  • Serous cystadenocarcinoma of the ovary
  • Meningioma

question: An elderly woman who was found to have an ovarian mass underwent staging laparotomy. Histopathological examination revealed the presence of Psammoma bodies. What is the most probable diagnosis?

explanationHtml:
The above clinical scenario and findings point to a diagnosis of pseudomyxoma peritonei. It is associated with mucinous cystadenoma.

Pseudomyxoma peritonei (PMP) is a rare condition that shows diffuse intra-abdominal gelatinous and mucoid material on peritoneal surfaces. Spontaneous perforation of a mucinous cystadenoma leads to implantation of low-grade malignant tumor cells in the peritoneum.

However, the most common cause of pseudomyxoma peritonei is carcinoma of the appendix.

Diagnosis is by CT, MRI, and laparoscopy. Even after the removal of the ovarian tumor, these cells continue to secrete mucin. Recurrence rates are high.
question: A 49-year-old woman presented with complaints of dull pain over the right lower abdomen for the past 2  months. CT scan revealed a left-sided multiloculated adnexal mass and exploratory laparotomy showed small mucoid implants scattered in the peritoneal cavity. Which of the following is associated with this condition?

explanationHtml:
The above scenario is suggestive of ovarian torsion. Mature cystic teratoma (dermoid cyst) is the commonest tumor to undergo torsion, especially at the end of the 1st trimester or during puerperium.

Management includes derotation and cystectomy in pregnancy irrespective of gestational age. This is also done in non-pregnant women of reproductive age to preserve ovarian function. Resection is reserved for patients in whom malignancy is suspected.

Dermoid cyst is the most common germ cell tumor. It is also the most common benign tumor of the ovary in the reproductive age group and in pregnancy. It is bilateral in 10-15% of cases.

Dermoid cyst is derived from all three germ cell layers, but ectodermal derivatives are most common. Rokitansky’s protuberance is the most common site for the development of malignancy. It is seen as a projection covered by skin, sebaceous glands, sweat glands, teeth, and bones. Sometimes thyroid tissue can be seen on histopathological examination, known as struma ovarii.

The image below shows a dermoid cyst with Rokitansky protuberance.
question: A 22-year-old woman at 14 weeks of gestation was rushed to the ER with complaints of severe abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. USG showed an edematous right ovary with a large cyst and disruption in adnexal flow on Doppler. Which of the following most commonly leads to this condition?

explanationHtml:
The given histopathological image shows Schiller-Duval bodies. It is suggestive of a yolk sac tumor (endodermal sinus tumor).

It is an aggressive malignant germ cell tumor of the ovaries. It occurs in ovaries or testes and sacrococcygeal areas in young children. It is usually unilateral. These tumors are usually associated with raised AFP and alpha 1 antitrypsin.

The image below depicts Schiller-Duval bodies. It consists of a central capillary surrounded by tumor cells, present within a cystic space that may be lined by flat to cuboidal tumor cells. 50% of yolk sac tumors have Schiller-Duval bodies and they are pathognomonic when present.
question: Staging laparotomy was performed in a teenage girl who presented with an adnexal mass. Histopathological examination showed the following. What is the diagnosis?

explanationHtml:
The counterpart of seminoma in females is dysgerminoma. It is a germ cell tumor.

It usually arises in young women or in children. It is the most common malignant germ cell tumor diagnosed during pregnancy. They account for approximately 1/3rd of all malignant ovarian germ cell tumors.

Serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and the isoenzymes LDH-1 and LDH-2 may be used in monitoring individuals or disease recurrence.

Treatment involves unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. It is highly radiosensitive and has a good prognosis.

Dysgerminoma was considered to be the most common malignant germ cell tumor of the ovary. Recent data indicates that in the past few decades, their incidence has reduced considerably. Immature teratomas are now the most common type of malignant germ cell tumor of the ovary.

The image below shows the histopathology of a dygerminoma, characterized by uniform cells resembling primordial germ cells separated by fibrous septa with lymphocytes.
question: What is the counterpart of seminoma in females?

explanationHtml:
Germ cell tumors are the most common ovarian tumor in women aged less than 20 years.

Epithelial tumours are the commonest tumours. It accounts for 80% of all ovarian malignant tumours.
question: The most common ovarian tumor in women less than 20 years of age is _____.

explanationHtml:
Non-mucinous cystadenocarcinoma is an epithelial tumor of the ovary. It has elevated CA- 125 levels.

CA-125 value > 35 U/ml is suggestive of epithelial ovarian cancer.

Malignant conditions with raised CA 125 levels:

  • Ovarian epithelial carcinoma (most common cause)
  • Endometrial cancer
  • Pancreatic cancer
  • Colon cancer
  • Breast cancer
  • Lung cancer
  • Lymphoma

Benign conditions with raised CA 125 levels:

  • Pregnancy
  • Pelvic inflammatory disease
  • Endometriosis
  • Uterine fibroid
  • Normally elevated in 1% females
  • Acute peritonitis
question: Which of the following tumors show raised CA-125 levels?

explanationHtml:
Lactate dehydrogenase is the tumor marker in dysgerminoma.

Dysgerminomas are primitive neoplasms. They are the only germ cell malignancy with a significant rate of bilateral ovarian involvement (15-20%).

It is seen in young women with an average incidence of 20 years of age. It is the most common malignant germ cell tumor diagnosed during pregnancy. They account for approximately 1/3rd of all malignant ovarian germ cell tumors.

It secretes placental alkaline phosphatase (PALP), lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), and β-hCG. Serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and the isoenzymes LDH-1 and LDH-2 may be used in monitoring individuals or disease recurrence.

Treatment involves unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. It is highly radiosensitive and has a good prognosis.
question: A young woman with an adnexal mass is diagnosed with dysgerminoma. Which of the following tumor markers are likely to be elevated in her?

explanationHtml:
Risk of malignancy index (RMI) score of 200 or more indicates a high risk for ovarian cancer in a patient with an adnexal mass.

Risk of malignancy index (RMI) = U x M x CA125

  • U = Ultrasound score
    • Metastases, solid areas, multilocular cysts, ascites, and bilateral lesions - These characteristics are each given 1 point
    • Scores:
      • U = 0 (for USG score of 0)
      • U = 1 (for USG score of 1)
      • U = 3 (for USG score of 2–5).
  • M = Menopausal status
    • M= 1 (for pre-menopausal)
    • M= 3 (for post-menopausal)
  • CA-125 = Serum CA-125 level (in IU/ml)

For any post-menopausal woman with an ovarian cyst of size >1cm, RMI should be calculated.
question: A post-menopausal woman is found to have an adnexal mass on evaluation. Above what risk of malignancy index (RMI) score is there a high risk of ovarian malignancy?

correctAnswer: D. It is not a malignant tumor
explanationHtml:
Brenner tumors are usually benign but rarely they can turn malignant.

Brenner tumor (transitional cell tumor) is a benign, epithelial, unilateral tumor, resembling a fibroma. Histologically, Walthard cell rests and coffee bean nuclei are seen.

Brenner tumor represent only 2-3% of all ovarian neoplasms, and <2% of these tumors are malignant.

It is called Meigs' syndrome if the clinical picture is caused by an ovarian fibroma, granulosa cell tumor, Brenner tumor, or thecoma.

Meig’s syndrome is characterized by a triad of:

  1. Benign ovarian tumor
  2. Ascites
  3. Right-sided pleural effusion.

Pseudo Meigs' syndrome is when the causative factor is ovarian secondaries, leiomyoma, and benign ovarian cysts such as teratoma and mucinous cystadenoma.

The image given below shows coffee bean nuclei.

Walthard cell rests and coffee bean nuclei are seen
It is not a malignant tumor

question: Which of the following statements is false regarding Brenner tumor?

correctAnswer: D. Oral contraceptive use is a risk factor
explanationHtml:
The above scenario points to a diagnosis of theca lutein cysts in association with molar pregnancy. Theca lutein cysts are not associated with the use of oral contraceptives.

Lutein cysts types :

  1. Granulosa lutein cysts - They occur due to failure of regression of corpus luteum after 14 days of ovulation.
  2. Theca lutein cysts - They are found in association with hydatidiform moles, choriocarcinoma, and gonadotropin (hCG), or clomiphene therapy.

Theca lutein cysts occur due to the hyperstimulation of ovaries as a result of high hCG levels in molar pregnancies and other conditions. They are usually bilateral.

These cysts usually regress spontaneously in a period of 2-4 months following the evacuation of a molar pregnancy.

Sometimes they can undergo torsion and cause marked pelvic pain. In such instances, laparoscopic untwisting of the cyst has to be done.

It is seen with clomiphene administration
Oral contraceptive use is a risk factor

question: A 31-year-old woman presenting with 12 weeks of amenorrhea and passage of vesicles per vagina is suspected to have a molar pregnancy. On transvaginal ultrasonography, the left ovary appears as shown below. Which of the statements is not true regarding this condition?

explanationHtml:
The above clinical scenario points to a diagnosis of granulosa cell tumor. It is associated with carcinoma endometrium.

Granulosa cell tumors cells are estrogen-secreting ovarian tumors. It is seen in 80% of women over 40 years and 5% of pre-pubertal girls. Precocious puberty is seen due to excess secretion of estrogen.

It is a low-grade malignancy. It is almost always unilateral. Tumor marker inhibin B is frequently elevated more than inhibin A. Surgical resection is the treatment of choice.

On histopathology, it has characteristic Call-Exner bodies. It appears as a rosette arrangement of cells around an eosinophilic fluid space, as shown below.

Inhibin A is elevated more than inhibin B

question: A woman noticed premature breast development in her 7-year-old daughter and brought her to the gynecology OPD. USG revealed a right-sided adnexal mass. The patient underwent laparotomy and the biopsy revealed Call-Exner bodies. Which of the following is true regarding this condition?

explanationHtml:
Prophylactic oophorectomy is indicated if one ovary has already been removed for benign neoplasm.

Candidates suitable for prophylactic oophorectomy:

  • Nulliparous aged > 45 years
  • Any age with a history of ovarian, endometrial, or colon cancer in a 1st-degree relative
  • Grossly abnormal ovary in the premenopausal age group
  • One ovary removed for benign neoplasm
  • Previous history of breast carcinoma

Abnormal ovary in reproductive age group woman

question: Which among the following high-risk patients are suitable for prophylactic oophorectomy?

explanationHtml:
Stage 3 ovarian cancer is a unilateral or bilateral ovarian tumor with pelvic lymph node and/or regional lymph node involvement and liver capsule involvement.

Grading of ovarian cancer:

  • Grade 1 - well-differentiated cancers have cells that closely resemble normal cells and are less likely to spread or recur.
  • Grade 2 - moderately differentiated cancer cells.
  • Grade 3 - poorly differentiated cancers show increasing abnormality of appearance compared to normal cells. They are also more likely to spread and recur.
question: A 63-year-old woman presented with complaints of pelvic and abdominal pain, and significant weight loss. On CT scan, a bilateral ovarian tumor with pelvic lymph node and liver capsule involvement was seen. What stage does this belong to?

explanationHtml: Unilateral oophorectomy is preferred in a young woman who has not completed her family in case of early-stage disease.
question: A 26-year-old nulliparous woman is diagnosed with early-stage ovarian cancer. Which surgery should be done in her case?

explanationHtml: Dysgerminoma is the most radiosensitive ovarian tumor. They are highly susceptible to radiotherapy.
question: Which of the following ovarian tumors is the most radiosensitive?

correctAnswer: D. CA- 125 level estimation; if normal, advise regular follow-up
explanationHtml:
CA-125 level measurement is the next best step according to the latest RCOG guidelines for post-menopausal ovarian cysts.

Management includes the following:

A pap smear is a screening test for cervical cancer. It is not a diagnostic test (option C). The presence of abnormal cells/ a positive test requires further evaluation by colposcopy, cervical biopsy, or fractional curettage.

Endometrial hyperplasia with atypia carries 29% risk of developing into endometrial carcinoma and hence, must be treated with total abdominal hysterectomy (simple hysterectomy ). The presence of any concomitant endometrial cancer must be ruled out by doing fractional curettage (or dilatation and curettage) before doing a hysterectomy.

If a premenopausal woman does not desire to undergo hysterectomy, progesterone can be given and the patient is followed up every 3-6 months. If the atypia persists during the follow-up hysterectomy should be performed.

The table below summarizes the management of patients with endometrial hyperplasia

Management of Endometrial hyperplasia
Hyperplasia without atypia
Pre-menopausal women Progesterone therapy
Postmenopausal women:
  • Simple hyperplasia without atypia
  • Complex hyperplasia without atypia

  • Follow up without therapy
  • Progesterone therapy
Hyperplasia with atypia
Pre-menopausal women

If patient wishes to preserve uterus,give High-dose progesterone therapy

If atypia persists, then perform Total abdominal hysterectomy
Peri-menopausal women Total abdominal hysterectomy
Post-menopausal women Total abdominal hysterectomy +BSO (bilateral salphingo-ophorectomy)
question: Which among the following is an ideal treatment for a 55-year-old female with simple hyperplasia of the endometrium with atypia?

explanationHtml:
In a postmenopausal woman with abnormal uterine bleeding(AUB), an endometrial thickness of >4 mm warrants further testing, such as an endometrial biopsy.

In postmenopausal women with AUB, endometrial thickness is correlated with the risk of cancer. However, if the thickness is ≤4 mm, the chances of malignancy are low. Such cases can be managed conservatively with tranexamic acid. Despite medical management, if the bleeding persists, invasive methods like fractional curettage and hysteroscopy or endometrial biopsy are required.

The algorithm for the next step for abnormal uterine bleeding in different age groups is as follows:

Age group Endometrial thickness on TVS Action
Age <40years >12mm Endometrial sampling/Endometrial biopsy
Age >40 years or Age >45 years - Endometrial sampling/Endometrial biopsy is done irrespective of USG findings
Post menopausal women >4mm Endometrial sampling/Endometrial biopsy
Post menopausal women <4mm
  • Reassurance+tranexamic acid
  • If bleeding persists, then do an endometrial biopsy

explanationHtml:
The most common variety of endometrial cancer is adenocarcinoma.

The other varieties of endometrial cancer are squamous cell, clear cell, and serous. The most malignant varieties are clear cell carcinoma and papillary serous tumor.
question: What is the most common histopathological variety of endometrial cancer?

explanationHtml:
Type 2 carcinoma endometrium is commonly seen in menopausal women with atrophic endometrium.

Histological classification of endometrial cancer:

Type 1 (Endometrioid) Type 2 (Nonendometriod)
Estrogen dependent Estrogen independent
Occurs in Pre- and Peri-menopausal women Occurs in post-menopausal women
Hyperplasia present Hyperplasia absent
Good prognosis Poor prognosis
Associated with PTEN/KRAS mutation Associated with p53 mutation

Note: Type 1 (estrogen-dependent) endometrial CA is the more common type.
question: Which of the following predisposes a patient to develop type 2 carcinoma endometrium?

explanationHtml:
Corpus cancer syndrome constitutes of:

  • Diabetes mellitus
  • Obesity
  • Hypertension
  • Cancer of the body of the uterus.

Etiology of endometrial carcinoma: (Mnemonic: Family Has OLD AUNTI)

  • Family history
  • Hypertension
  • Obesity
  • Late menopause/Early menarche
  • Diabetes
  • Atypical endometrial hyperplasia
  • Unopposed estrogen/increased estrogen → Hormone replacement therapy, fibroid, PCOD
  • Nulliparous
  • Tamoxifen therapy (Raloxifene has no genito-urinary action)
  • Infertility/irregular menses.

Protective factors against endometrial carcinoma include the use of OCPs, smoking, and multiparity.

explanationHtml:
The image depicts saline infusion sonography (SIS), also known as sonohysterography. It is usually done after a transvaginal ultrasound, to assess the detailed anatomy of the uterine cavity.

In this procedure, a balloon catheter is inserted through the cervix and the endometrial cavity is distended with 20-40ml of sterile saline. The balloon is inflated to block the backflow of the infused sterile saline and transvaginal ultrasound is performed to visualize the cavity.

It is used:

  • To determine the endometrial thickness
  • To determine the cause in cases of infertility
  • To identify Mullerian anomalies
  • To visualize endometrial polyps and pedunculated fibroids

The image given below shows the appearance of the uterus on SIS.

Option A: Transvaginal ultrasound is the initial evaluation for postmenopausal bleeding.

Option B: In balloon endometrial ablation, a balloon is inserted into the uterus and inflated with glycine or 5% glucose. It is then heated up, and the endometrium is ablated by the tamponade effect.

Option D: In hysterosalpingography, contrast dye is inserted into the uterus via a catheter, and the uterine and fallopian tube anatomy is visualized.
question: A gynecologist is performing the following procedure in a woman with postmenopausal bleeding. Identify it.

explanationHtml:
Decreased vascular resistance with increased tumor vascularity is seen in carcinoma endometrium.

USG findings in carcinoma endometrium include:

  • Endometrial thickness >4 mm in postmenopausal women and >10 mm in perimenopausal women
  • Hyperechoic endometrium with irregular outlines
  • Increased tumor vascularity with low vascular resistance
  • Fluid in uterine cavity
question: A menopausal patient suspected to have endometrial carcinoma is undergoing a transvaginal ultrasound. Which of the following findings would be inconsistent with her diagnosis?

explanationHtml:
The next line of management in a patient with increased endometrial thickness is an endometrial biopsy.

In a postmenopausal woman, the normal endometrium should not exceed 4 mm in thickness. If it exceeds 4 mm, then histopathological examination (HPE) of the endometrium is mandatory, irrespective of the presence or absence of symptoms. In a perimenopausal woman, the cutoff for normal endometrial thickness is 10mm.

Hysteroscopy and biopsy is preferred over other blind curettage methods for HPE. A biopsy is made from suspicious areas after visualization so chances of missing the lesion are reduced.
question: A 52-year-old woman with postmenopausal bleeding has an endometrial thickness of 7 mm on ultrasound. What is the next step in her management?

explanationHtml:
Hysteroscopic inspection and selective biopsy is now considered the gold standard in the diagnosis of an endometrial lesion. It is preferred for the initial evaluation of women with bleeding suspicious for malignancy.

Endometrial sampling can be done by hysteroscopic biopsy. It is more sensitive for focal endometrial lesions. Dilatation and curettage may also aid the sampling of endometrial lesions.

Ultrasound, CT, and MRI are adjuvant to other investigations. Diagnostic laparoscopy will be required to study the nature of the tumor and its spread if ultrasound picks up a pelvic tumor.

The image given below shows the procedure of hysteroscopy.
question: A 54-year-old woman with postmenopausal bleeding is suspected to have an endometrial lesion. What is the gold standard investigation to confirm her diagnosis?

explanationHtml:
The given scenario depicts endometrial carcinoma and the gold standard method for staging this condition is surgery.

The established staging procedure for endometrial cancer is a comprehensive surgery involving a total hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and dissection of the pelvic and para-aortic lymph nodes. This is as defined by the FIGO/TNM classification system.

Option A: To detect myometrial invasion or cervical involvement, contrast-enhanced MRI is the best modality.

Option C: Hysteroscopy visualizes the entire uterine lining and a biopsy is taken from suspicious areas. This is not 100% predictive, as an early lesion can be missed. Recently, the concern has been raised regarding the spilling of cancer cells into the peritoneal cavity during hysteroscopy.

Option D: PET–CT reveals metabolic activity in the tissue and is highly sensitive and specific for detecting positive pelvic and/or para-aortic lymphadenopathy as well as distant metastases in selected high-risk patients with endometrial cancer.
question: A 62-year-old woman presents with vaginal bleeding 11 years after she had attained menopause. An endometrial biopsy reveals adenocarcinoma. What is the gold standard method for staging her condition?

explanationHtml:
Pelvic and para-aortic lymph nodes are commonly involved in endometrial cancer.

The spread is through the infundibulopelvic ligament.

Rarely, inguinal & femoral lymph nodes are involved.
question: Which lymph nodes are most commonly involved in patients with endometrial carcinoma?

explanationHtml: Carcinoma endometrium involving the vagina but having no lymph node involvement is classified as stage IIIB.
question: A patient presented with carcinoma endometrium involving >50% myometrium, extending to the vagina but with no involvement of para-aortic and pre aortic nodes. What is the stage of her disease?

correctAnswer: A. Hysterectomy, B/L salpingo-oophorectomy, lymph node sampling
explanationHtml:
Early endometrial cancer (stages I & II) is primarily managed surgically. The surgery performed here is abdominal hysterectomy, B/L salpingo-oophorectomy, omentectomy and pelvic & para-aortic lymph node sampling.

Postoperative management of endometrial cancer:

In low-risk endometrial cancer, no further treatment is required.

In intermediate-risk, radiotherapy is done.

In high risk, chemotherapy + radiotherapy is done.

options.text: Hysterectomy, B/L salpingo-oophorectomy, lymph node sampling

question: Which of the following is indicated for the treatment of a patient with early endometrial cancer?

correctAnswer: A. Intensity is inversely proportional to squared distance
explanationHtml:
The intensity of radiation is inversely proportional to the squared distance. This is known as the inverse square law in radiotherapy.

Chemoradiation is the mainstay of treatment of stage III and IV endometrial cancers. They are treated with brachytherapy followed by external radiation. Brachytherapy is a form of radiation therapy in which the radiation source is placed close to the tumor.

Other options:

Option B: Larger blood vessels are more radioresistant than microvasculature.

Option C: Permanent non-dividing cells are more radioresistant than rapidly proliferating cells.

Option D: Small intestinal epithelial cells (intestinal crypts), which divide rapidly with no differentiation are the most radiosensitive.

options.text: Intensity is inversely proportional to squared distance
Small blood vessels are most radioresistant
Rapidly proliferating cells are most radioresistant

question: A woman with endometrial carcinoma is undergoing radiotherapy. Which of the following is true?

explanationHtml:
Chemotherapy is the mainstay of treatment in Stage III endometrial cancer.

In order to stage carcinoma endometrium, total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and lymphadenectomy is done (surgical staging).

Thus the management, once staging is done, is mainly postoperative. Up to stage II, radiotherapy can be given. Stages III & IV are managed by chemotherapy such as doxorubicin, cisplatin, and paclitaxel.

Note: Stage III is said to be inoperable but debulking surgery is sometimes attempted. However, the mainstay of treatment for stage III disease remains chemotherapy.

The image shows a cardiotocograph (electronic fetal monitor) that is used to perform cardiotocography in labor.

It can be used in both antenatal and intranatal mothers. It measures fetal heart rate and uterine contractions. It is used to perform the non-stress test (NST) in the antenatal period and cardiotocography during labor.
question: You notice the following instrument being used to monitor a primigravida in the first stage of labor.  What is the investigation being performed here?

explanationHtml:
This is an image of cervidil vaginal insert. It is used for cervical ripening and improves the Bishop's score.

It contains 10 mg of dinoprostone designed to release at a rate of approximately 0.3 mg/hr over 10-hours.
question: During your OBG posting, one of the senior residents asks you to induce labor in a primigravida admitted at 40 weeks of gestation. Identify the following device that you can use for this purpose.

explanationHtml:
The given instrument is Kocher's artery forceps and is identified by the presence of a single tooth at the tip.

Kocher's artery forceps are used to achieve hemostasis by holding bleeding vessels. They are also used in low rupture of membranes to augment labour or for the surgical induction of labour.

The difference between artery forceps and needle holders is in the edge and smoothness of corrugations. Artery forceps have smooth edges and single lined corrugations whereas, needle holders have rough edges and crossed lines forming square to diamond shaped corrugations.
question: The following instrument is used to augment labour in a 28-year-old primigravida via low rupture of membranes. Identify this instrument.

explanationHtml:
The given scenario of prolonged second stage of labor can be managed by performing an episiotomy. In the given figure, the instrument marked as "D" corresponds to episiotomy scissors.

An episiotomy is done to prevent posterior extention leading to obstetric anal sphincteric injuries.
question: A primigravida was diagnosed with a prolonged second stage of labor due to the fetus being in occipitoposterior position. The obstetrician decided to give a posterior mediolateral cut at the introitus to facilitate delivery. Which of the following instruments would she use for the same?

correctAnswer: B. It can be used to deliver aftercoming head in breech.
explanationHtml:
The given image shows Wrigley's forceps.

These are used as outlet forceps for the extraction of the fetal head. It is used to provide traction force. It can also be used in C-section for delivery of the baby.

The instrument is light and short due to a reduction in the length of the shanks and handles. It has a marked cephalic curve with a slight pelvic curve.

Conditions that require to be fulfilled for the use of outlet forceps are:

  • The fetal scalp is visible without separating the labia (crowning)
  • The fetal skull has reached the pelvic floor, or is on the perineum
  • The sagittal suture is in the anteroposterior diameter or right or left occiput anterior or posterior position (rotation does not exceed 45°)

Note: Delivery of aftercoming head in breech is done with Pipers forceps.

options.text: It can be used in caesarean sections.
It can be used to deliver aftercoming head in breech.
It is a type of outlet forceps.

question: The following instrument is used on an exhausted primigravida during crowning of the fetal head. Which of the following is false about this instrument?

explanationHtml:
The given instrument is Green-Armytage forceps.

Its tips are broad and hence can compress a wide area. During lower segment caesarean section (LSCS), these forceps are applied at the bleeding cut uterine edges for hemostasis.
question: While assisting in the caesarean section of a multigravida, you see the senior obstetrician using the following instrument. Identify it.

explanationHtml:
The instrument is Karman’s cannula and syringe, which is also used for menstrual regulation.

Menstrual regulation is the aspiration of the endometrial cavity within 14 days of a missed period in a woman with a previous normal cycle.

Under aseptic precautions, the cervix may be gently dilated using 4-5 mm size dilators. Then 5-6mm Karman’s cannula is inserted and attached to a 50ml syringe for suction. The cannula is rotated, and pushed in and out with gentle strokes.

This procedure is contraindicated in advanced pregnancy and in the presence of local pelvic inflammation. The drawbacks of the procedure include a missed implanted zygote or an unrecognized ectopic pregnancy.

This procedure is not commonly done anymore.
question: An obstetrician performs an aspiration of the endometrial cavity in a woman with complaints of a missed period 2 weeks back. Identify the following instrument. What is the procedure it is used for?

explanationHtml:
The image shows a manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) syringe.

Manual vacuum aspiration can be safely done upto 12 weeks of gestation. However, WHO recommends it as the procedure of choice for MTP only upto 10 weeks of gestation .

The indications of this procedure are given as follows:

  • Medical termination of pregnancy
  • Incomplete abortion or missed abortion
  • Molar pregnancy
  • Endometrial aspiration
question: A 20-year-old woman at 9 weeks of gestation comes to the clinic for check-up following an MTP. On ultrasound, retained tissue was found and the following instrument was used for its removal. What is this instrument?

The given image shows Hegar's double-ended dilator which is used to dilate the cervix in dilation and curettage procedure.

Pratt dilator is also a double-ended dilator but has a more linear shape as compared to the curved Hegar's dilators. The image given below shows a Pratt dilator.

Option A: Hawkin dilator is a single-ended dilator. The image given below shows a Hawkin dilator.

Option C: Bakes rosebud dilator is a single-ended dilator used to dilate the urethra. It is called so since its tip is similar to a rosebud. The image given below shows a Bakes dilator.

question: Identify the following instrument that is commonly used in a dilatation and curettage procedure.

explanationHtml:
The image shows a Fenton dilator. These can be identified by the neck/notch at the centre.

Fenton's or modified Fenton's procedure is performed to widen the introitus in women with superficial dyspareunia secondary to scarring. The narrowing of introitus could be due to scarring secondary to perineal tears during childbirth or from conditions such as lichen sclerosus or vestibulitis.

Fenton dilators come in sizes numbered from 3-10 and the sizes of the dilators range from 3mm to 26mm.

Option B: Hawkins dilator is single-ended.

Options A and C: Hegar and Pratt dilators are also double-ended dilators but they do not have a notch at the centre. Pratt dilator is more linear in appearance compared to Hegar dilator.
question: A 25-year-old woman presents with dyspareunia due to scarring secondary to perineal tears from previous vaginal delivery. The gynaecologist advises the use of the following dilator to widen the introitus. Identify this instrument.

explanationHtml:
The instrument shown in the image is Sim's curette. It is a single-ended uterine curette used for dilatation and curettage.

It is designed to remove tough tissue from the lining of the uterus for biopsy or excision. The curette features a sharp loop tip to aid in the removal of the uterine tissue.
question: You have posted a 43-year-old woman with abnormal uterine bleeding for dilatation and curettage in the minor OT.  Identify the following instrument used in this procedure.

explanationHtml:

question: The following instrument is used for all except:

correctAnswer: C. It retracts the posterior vaginal wall to expose the cervix
explanationHtml:
The given instrument is Simpson’s uterine sound. It is not used to retract the vagina for cervical examination. This is done using Sim's speculum.

The instrument is held like a pencil with the thumb and the first 2 fingers and introduced into the uterine cavity by keeping it in the midline and ensuring it is not forced.

The uses are given as follows:

  • To measure uterine cavity and cervical length
  • To diagnose cervical stenosis
  • To sound a polyp, IUCD or uterine septum
  • To break adhesions
  • To differentiate between chronic inversion and fibroid polyp

question: Which of the following is a false statement about the instrument given below?

question: You see a resident use the following instrument to grasp the anterior lip of the cervix in a patient posted for a vaginal hysterectomy. What is this instrument known as?

The given instrument is a towel-holding clip. It is used to secure drapings and towels during surgery.

Sponge-holding forceps are non-traumatic forceps. They are used for painting and preparation of parts preoperatively.

Filshie clips are used for laparoscopic tubal sterilisation. They are made of titanium on the outer side and sialistic material on the inner side.
question: Identify the following instrument.

question: Identify the instrument.

explanationHtml:
The image shows an endocervical brush. It is used to collect samples from the endocervix cervix, especially from deep lesions.

Option A: Cervex brush is ideal for collecting samples for liquid-based cytological studies.

question: Your senior resident uses the following instrument while performing a pap smear test for screening of cervical cancer in a 36-year-old woman. Identify the same.

Sharpness on the end can differentiate between Ayre's and Aylesbury spatula. Aylesbury spatula has a more sharp and longer tip than Ayer's spatula. So, Aylesbury spatula is superior to Ayre's in collecting endocervical samples.

question: A 32-year-old working IT professional came for a mobile cervical cancer screening camp planned at her workplace. What is the following instrument used to perform this screening test?

correctAnswer: D. External os is visualised at a distance of 50 cm
explanationHtml:
The device shown in the image is a colposcope. It is used to perform colposcopy where the cervix is visualized at a distance of around 20 cm with the patient in the lithotomy position.

This instrument provides binocular vision with a magnification of 6x-15x. A green filter is used to study vascular pattern as the vessels appear black. Abnormal areas can be identified by their peculiar vascular pattern such as mosaic, reticular, and punctate.

question: A 35-year-old lady who had tested positive for HPV  is undergoing an investigation where the following device is used. Which of the following statements is false about this investigation?

question: The following instrument is used for a young lady with fibroids posted for open myomectomy. Identify it.

explanationHtml:
The given instrument is a fallope ring applicator. It is used in tubal ligation.

Falope ring sterilization is accomplished by applying silicone rubber bands to the fallopian tubes. The major advantage is the elimination of thermocoagulation. The occlusion is only in a short segment and can allow for tubal reconstruction.
